title: Comparison of Majorization Relations for Probability Vectors
statement: For probability vectors $x,y$ with nonzero coordinates, write $x\prec_C y$ if $x\otimes z\prec y\otimes z$ for some probability vector $z$, and write $x\prec_M y$ if $x^{\otimes n}\prec y^{\otimes n}$ for some $n\geq1$. The conditions $N_p(x)\leq N_p(y)$ for $p\geq1$, $N_p(x)\geq N_p(y)$ for $0\leq p\leq1$, and $N_p(x)\leq N_p(y)$ for $p\leq0$, where $N_p(u)=\sum_i u_i^p$, characterize when $x$ is an $\ell^1$-limit of vectors $x_k\prec_C y$. Do the same conditions characterize when $x$ is an $\ell^1$-limit of vectors $x_k\prec_M y$?
